failure_summary: Render-layer defect on two fronts: the offered term immediate_threat (canonicalPhrase "threat to make four next move") is board-false for c3r2 on its own truthBoard `decision` — visualize_board on 33343064336444661500146 shows col3 ht=0 so c3r2 is [X] NON-gravity-top and only becomes <X> [GT] after the played move (333430643364446615001462), and the prompt frame itself hedges it as "not yet reachable — the column needs to fill first" — so the model echoing the offered phrase produced an A4 fabrication; separately the L3 guardrail ("MUST NOT say the played move caused or enabled the pattern") forbids the only actionable cause on this board (column 3 lands at c3r1, directly under the opponent's threat square, making it playable at once), leaving the model with nothing but the frame's own outcome restatement "only speeds up the finish" → A7a on both runs.
notes: n_runs=2 (per dispatch), so no axis was sub-sampled — every axis was graded on both runs; no nulls. BOARD TRUTH: decision board 33343064336444661500146 has opponent (X/P1) major threats at col3 row2 and col6 row3, both NON-gravity-top (col3 ht=0). afterBest 333430643364446615001460 keeps c3r2 non-gravity-top (solver +3..+5 for X). afterPlayed 333430643364446615001462 makes c3r2 <X> [GT] with solver col3 = 9 (win-in-1). A4 fail (both runs): servedExplanation asserts "next-move four at column 3, row 2" — false on the decision board it is anchored to; the opponent cannot play c3r2 until c3r1 fills. The wording is render-supplied (offered term canonicalPhrase), so render_bug, not prompt_confusion. A7 fail on A7a (both runs): the served prose gives no cause — run 0 "speeds things up by giving your opponent an easier follow-up", run 1 "gives them a cleaner follow-up and speeds up the finish" — pure outcome restatement; the true cause is blocked by the L3 guardrail. A7b passes (c3r2, the c2r1-c3r2-c4r3-c5r4 diagonal, and column 1 are all named in prose); A7c N/A (mechanism is not a fork); A7d passes (named idea plus the squares that instantiate it). A3 passes: the opponent diagonal c2r1(X17)-c3r2(empty)-c4r3(X3)-c5r4(X13) is real and IS the decisive reason. A5 passes: 2nd person, no player names, no internal field names; A5b does not apply (player=2 but boardState="mid-game"). G4 passes: every named cell verified against render_decision.finalMovestring 333430643364446615001462. G5 passes: all rendered threat-list entries are board-true on their stated boards. G6 passes: patternOnAfterBestBoard=true is correct (c3r2 [X] present on afterBest), so L3 is the right route. G2 passes: guardrail honored (no causation claim, no "you are lost", no defeatist closing clause, toughest-defense frame kept); confidence is "high" so L9 hedging does not apply. G3 passes: nothing in the answer needed the omitted afterBest board (its tag set is identical to the decision board). G7 FAIL (judgment half, both runs): membership is clean (mechanical G7a/G7b pass, annotationRepairs empty, roles matched — opp-major on square words, opp-major-line on line words, term and zone adjacent not nested), BUT the render_decision.requiredSet handle `better-col` is emitted in NEITHER run, although the assembled prompt says "Every handle listed below MUST appear ... Do not omit any of these"; "column 1 is the tougher defense" ships unwrapped, so the better move is never highlighted on the board. Recording this under G7 is a judgment call — v1 enumerates only role-match / over-wrap / annotationRepairs — but leaving a hard render-contract MUST unrecorded on every axis would be worse; flagged here for orchestrator normalisation. Secondary render defect, unused by the model: alias `opp-double` has role "the single fork square where your opponent gets two winning squares at once" but spec "windows:c3r2,c6r3" is the two winning squares, not a pivot. MODEL REGIME: rows are gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships — this is a PRODUCTION-FIDELITY run, not a floor test. Both attributions above are model-INDEPENDENT (a board-false offered term; a guardrail that suppresses the cause), so no prompt_confusion bucket is claimed.

counterexamples.evidence: canonicalPhrase is "threat to make four next move" and it is offered alongside zone opp-major whose truthBoard is `decision`; visualize_board 33343064336444661500146 shows col3 ht=0 and marks c3r2 as [X] (non-gravity), not <X> [GT] — the threat is only immediate on opponentPunishment.finalMovestring 333430643364446615001462. Both runs wrote "next-move four at column 3, row 2". The prompt's own reading key forbids exactly this upgrade, so the render contradicts itself.

The guardrail forbids saying the played move "caused or enabled the pattern", but on this board the played column 3 lands at c3r1 — directly under the opponent threat square c3r2 — turning a non-gravity threat into <X> [GT] (solver col3 = 9, win-in-1 on 333430643364446615001462). The one transferable lesson is the one the guardrail blocks, so both runs fall back to the frame's own "only speeds up the finish".

Neither run emitted [zone:better-col]; run 0 raw uses only opp-major and opp-major-line, run 1 the same. The assembled prompt states "Every handle listed below MUST appear ... Do not omit any of these". Required-set enforcement exists in production via the retry path, which this harness does not exercise (OI-183).

Role text says "the single fork square where your opponent gets two winning squares at once" while the spec is a two-cell window c3r2,c6r3 — those are the two winning squares, not a pivot. Unused by the model here, but the role would mis-instruct any answer that used it.
